artboards.title: Sign in — the frame around Clerk

annotations.text:
PLACEHOLDERS — nothing here is invented.

The brand has no name yet, so the wordmark reads [BRAND] and is a tweak chip: type your real name and it updates the nav, the footer and the copyright at once.

Same for [YOUR WHATSAPP NUMBER], [YOUR EMAIL], [YOUR LAGOS ADDRESS] and [ADD-ON PRICE]. The Lagos address is worth filling — the brief calls a physical address the cheapest credibility win available.

Product images are drawn placeholders. Swap them for real photos from a seeded demo store before this goes near a customer; nothing sells a garment like the garment.

SEO, baked in rather than bolted on.

One h1 per page, h2 per section, h3 per FAQ answer. No headline is an image. Every SVG carries a label or is marked decorative.

Copy targets what a seller actually types into Google — 'how much does an online store cost in Nigeria', 'sell online with Paystack', 'online store for my business Lagos' — rather than the words we would use internally.

The FAQ block is the highest-value SEO section on the page: six real questions, answers visible in the DOM (no accordion hiding them), ready for FAQPage structured data.

The head tags, JSON-LD, sitemap and OG image work is written up in docs/design/SEO-PLAN.md.

THE SCREENSHOT ASSET.

The brief says the distribution mechanic is someone screenshotting a page and forwarding it on WhatsApp. This is the screen designed for that: one phone frame, nothing scrolls, and the domain appears twice — once at the top, once beside the button — so a screenshot with no surrounding context still says where to go.

Dark ground on purpose: it survives being posted into a light or dark chat thread without dissolving.

Export it as PNG and it is ready to send.

TWO PRICING MODELS. Pick one; do not ship both.

Model A (above, 'Pricing — one price') is the package as the pricing doc settled it: one prominent figure, inclusions, add-ons, and the brochure-site comparison that justifies the number.

Model B (this one) is subscription-first: a free tier that pays us a share of sales, and paid plans that take 0%. It converts a build-fee treadmill into recurring revenue and its free tier removes the price objection entirely at the top of the funnel.

Every figure on both boards is a tweak chip. They are sample numbers, not a recommendation about your price — type your own and see which layout still reads well.

Model B needs schema and billing work that does not exist yet. Model A can ship on what is already built.

CLERK — tokens, not a pixel comp.

We do not own the markup inside the card, so treat everything in it as a spec for Clerk's appearance API rather than something to hand-build.

variables: colorPrimary #4DBF7D, colorText #0F2518, colorTextSecondary #7C8083, colorBackground #FFFFFF, colorInputBackground #FFFFFF, colorDanger #D42620, colorSuccess #04802E, borderRadius 4px, fontFamily the body face, fontSize 15.5px.

elements: card -> shadow-none border-0 p-0 bg-transparent (our own card wraps it); header and footer -> hidden (we render the title and the 'New here?' line); formButtonPrimary -> h-12 rounded bg-primary hover:bg-primary-600 shadow-btn normal-case; formFieldInput -> h-[46px] rounded border-grey-100 focus:border-primary; socialButtonsBlockButton -> h-[46px] rounded border-grey-100.

The left panel gradient is the app's own --background-image-sidebar, unchanged.

One real note from the build: Clerk's bot protection blocks automated sign-up, so this screen has never been driven end to end. Worth a manual pass once styled.
